name: Month-end close: settlement reconciliation and management accounts
trigger: monthly, on the close calendar date | event: a settlement cycle ends
human_role: the bookkeeper closing the month
inputs_required: brand brain: chart of accounts and cost classification tree

steps.name: Pull the month's raw exports
steps.does: Pull Shopify and marketplace orders, gateway settlement files, courier COD remittance files and the accounting export for the close month.
steps.output: raw export set with row counts per source
steps.check: every source file is present and dated inside the close month
steps.ask_founder_if: a source connector has no read access yet

steps.name: Reconcile the gateway settlement
steps.does: Unbundle each gateway payout into gross sale, fee, refund, GST on the fee and net, then match it to the bank credit.
steps.output: gateway reconciliation table with a named cause per gap
steps.check: every payout ties to a bank credit within 2 days or is flagged aged

steps.name: Reconcile marketplace settlements
steps.does: Unbundle commission, fixed fee, shipping fee, TCS under Section 52, GST on fees and refunds for each marketplace payout.
steps.output: marketplace reconciliation table, one row per payout
steps.check: TCS and GST on fees are broken out on their own lines, never netted into one number

steps.name: Reconcile COD cash and courier remittance
steps.does: Age cash on delivery collected by each courier against what has actually reached the bank, by courier.
steps.check: every remittance stuck past the courier's own SLA cycle is flagged with an escalation note and a named contact

steps.name: Reconcile ad platform invoices to logged spend
steps.does: Match the Meta and Google invoice amounts for the month to the spend the dashboards report.
steps.output: ad spend reconciliation line with variance
steps.check: any gap over 1 percent has a named cause, never left as rounding

steps.name: Build the evidence pack for each open dispute
steps.does: Assemble the order record, delivery proof, OTP log and support chat for each open gateway chargeback or UPI dispute, and check its filing deadline.
steps.output: one evidence pack per open dispute, with a filing deadline
steps.check: no dispute is missing its filing deadline
steps.ask_founder_if: a dispute needs a person to submit it through the gateway's own portal

steps.name: Update the fixed asset register
steps.does: Log any new capital purchase this month (equipment, fixtures, website build cost, packaging dies) and run the depreciation schedule.
steps.output: updated register with this month's depreciation line
steps.check: every asset carries purchase date, useful life and a running balance

steps.name: Run the cost classification and P&L ladder
steps.does: Apply the fixed decision tree for COGS, cost of delivery, marketing cost and OPEX, and build the ladder from gross revenue to net profit.
steps.check: every line traces to a source; no line is double-counted between COGS and OPEX

steps.name: Draft the settlement journal entries
steps.does: Draft one journal entry per settlement from the unbundled lines, instead of one lump bank deposit.
steps.output: draft journal entries for the accountant to post
steps.check: each entry's lines sum exactly to its bank credit

steps.name: Run the close checklist
steps.does: Run bank reconciliations, accrual review, inventory valuation and deferred revenue checks.
steps.output: close checklist, pass or fail per item
steps.check: no open item is left without an owner and a target date

steps.name: Diff against last month
steps.does: Compare the ladder and every reconciliation line to the prior month and name the single biggest change.
steps.output: one paragraph naming the biggest change and its cause
steps.check: the paragraph names a cause, not only a number

steps.name: Publish the management accounts
steps.does: Package the ladder, the reconciliation bridge and dispute status into the monthly management accounts report.
steps.check: every number carries a source and a freshness stamp

steps.name: Route unresolved items
steps.does: Send anything needing a signature, a gateway portal action or a judgment call outside the cost tree to the founder or bookkeeper.
steps.check: every unresolved item has a named owner and a date
steps.ask_founder_if: an accrual judgment call is not covered by the current cost classification tree

outputs: reconciliation bridge (gateway, marketplace, COD, ad invoices)
qa: every number sourced and freshness stamped
no missing value shown as zero
no ad account write attempted
GST and TCS never netted into one line
read_point: on publish, against last month's ladder and the annual budget
typical_duration: agent: 2 to 3 hours across the steps; waiting: up to 2 days for settlement files and accountant sign-off

name: Weekly contribution margin, SKU and customer profitability
trigger: weekly (margin, SKU) | quarterly (customer profitability, or before a loyalty tier redesign)
human_role: the finance analyst running the margin report
inputs_required: brand brain: SKU cost lines, product/SKU list
order export with channel and basket detail

steps.name: Pull orders, costs and support cost
steps.does: Pull the week's orders with SKU, basket and channel detail, landed cost per SKU, support ticket cost, return cost and discount cost.
steps.check: every order has a channel tag and every SKU has a landed cost

steps.name: Compute CM1, CM2 and CM3
steps.does: Compute CM1 (after COGS), CM2 (after delivery cost) and CM3 (after marketing cost), each labeled by scope.
steps.output: CM1/CM2/CM3 by basket, SKU and channel
steps.check: no margin number is shown without its scope label

steps.name: Classify each SKU
steps.does: Classify every SKU as champion, hidden gem, growth driver or underperformer on contribution and cash tied up.
steps.output: ranked SKU contribution table with a classification tag
steps.check: every SKU has exactly one classification

steps.name: Flag rationalization candidates
steps.does: Flag SKUs that are both cash-heavy and low-contribution for rationalization review.
steps.check: each candidate lists its contribution, cash tied up and last-90-day sell-through

steps.name: Add support, return and discount cost per customer
steps.does: Add support-ticket cost, return and refund cost, shipping cost and discount cost against each customer's revenue, in code.
steps.check: no cost bucket is estimated; a missing bucket shows as unavailable

steps.name: Feed loyalty tiering
steps.does: Rank customers by true profitability, not revenue, and flag mismatches against the current loyalty tier.
steps.check: every flagged customer shows the gap between tier and true profitability
steps.ask_founder_if: a tier redesign would move a named VIP customer down

steps.name: Diff against the prior period
steps.does: Compare this period's CM, SKU classifications and customer profitability to the last run.
steps.check: every named change states the driver, not just the delta

steps.name: Publish the standing report
steps.does: Publish the CM, SKU and customer profitability report so nobody guesses what a margin number includes.
steps.check: every figure states CM1, CM2 or CM3 explicitly

qa: margin scope always labeled
no revenue shown where profit was asked for
missing cost bucket shown as unavailable, not zero
read_point: weekly for CM and SKU; quarterly for customer profitability, against the prior run
typical_duration: agent: 45 to 90 minutes; no material waiting time

name: Price and promo economics gate
trigger: event: new SKU or cost change | event: a promo is proposed
human_role: the founder's pricing and promotions check
inputs_required: brand brain: net-profit target, landed cost
metric contract: current CM by SKU

steps.name: Take the net-profit target
steps.does: Read the brand's net-profit target for the SKU or line, never a keystone rule of thumb.
steps.check: the target came from the brand brain, not an assumed default

steps.name: Solve the price waterfall
steps.does: Solve bottom-up from landed cost through fees, shipping, returns and marketing cost to the shelf price that hits the target.
steps.output: proposed shelf price with full waterfall
steps.check: the waterfall shows every line between cost and price, none skipped

steps.name: Or model the promo economics
steps.does: For a proposed promo (percent-off, BOGO, gift-with-purchase, flash sale), model its real cost shape through the same waterfall.
steps.check: the model uses the promo's real mechanic, not a flat percent-off assumption

steps.name: Run the break-even check
steps.does: Run a break-even go/no-go check on the promo, or a margin stress-test on the new price.
inputs: promo cost model or price waterfall
steps.output: go/no-go recommendation with the break-even volume
steps.check: the recommendation states the exact volume or margin needed to break even

steps.name: Stress-test 60 to 90 days out
steps.does: For a new price, stress-test it against 60 to 90 days of actual sell-through once live.
steps.check: the stress-test uses real sell-through, not the launch-day forecast

steps.name: Write the founder brief
steps.does: Write the recommendation, the numbers behind it and the risk, with an explicit approve, reject or park line.
steps.check: the brief states the number the founder is approving, not just a description

steps.name: Stop for approval
steps.does: Stop before the price or promo goes public. Do not draft the site or ad copy change until approved.
steps.check: no downstream artefact is drafted before this step returns approved
steps.ask_founder_if: always: this capability is founder_gate

qa: profit target never replaced by keystone
TCS, GST and fee lines all present in the waterfall
no live change without recorded approval
read_point: 60 to 90 days after a price goes live, or the day after a promo ends
typical_duration: agent: 30 to 60 minutes; waiting: founder decision turnaround

name: Cash forecast, inventory planning and financing evaluation
trigger: weekly (forecast, inventory) | on demand (financing evaluation)
human_role: the person planning cash for the next quarter
inputs_required: brand brain: bank balance, payroll calendar, supplier lead times

steps.name: Pull cash inputs
steps.does: Pull the bank balance, payroll calendar, supplier lead times, inventory on order and the ad spend plan.
steps.check: all five inputs present or named as unavailable

steps.name: Build the 13-week forecast
steps.does: Build a rolling 13-week cash forecast from the inputs.
steps.check: the forecast never lets inventory cash go negative

steps.name: Reconcile profit to free cash flow
steps.does: Reconcile this month's profit to free cash flow and name the gap.
steps.check: the bridge names each of the 4 hidden cash traps checked

steps.name: Flag the lowest cash point
steps.does: Flag the lowest projected cash week before it happens, with a sensitivity range.
steps.check: the flag fires at least 3 weeks before the low point

steps.name: Roll inventory cash forward
steps.does: Roll inventory forward with lead time to plan cash, targeting days-of-inventory to supplier lead time.
steps.check: days-of-inventory is compared to lead time explicitly, not left implicit

steps.name: Manage the cash conversion cycle
steps.does: Track days inventory, days payable and days receivable together as the cash conversion cycle.
steps.output: cash conversion cycle number with trend
steps.check: the cycle is shown as one number with its 3 parts, not only the parts

steps.name: Compare financing options
steps.does: When cash runs low or a hard-to-source launch needs funding, compare real borrowing options (line of credit, inventory financing, revenue-based) and, for a hard-to-fund launch, crowdfunding, private capital or manufacturer referrals, against reference cost-of-capital rates.
steps.check: every option shows its real cost of capital, not the advertised rate

steps.name: Stress-test repayments
steps.does: Stress-test any financing option's repayment schedule against a slower-sales scenario.
steps.check: the stress case uses the brand's own slow-month history, not a generic haircut

steps.name: Write the founder brief and stop
steps.does: Write the recommendation and stop for approval before any financing commitment or launch spend is signed.
steps.check: no financing or sourcing commitment is treated as decided by this agent
steps.ask_founder_if: always: financing evaluation and sourcing decisions are human_assist

qa: inventory never modeled negative
profit and cash reconciled monthly
financing cost shown at its real rate
read_point: weekly against the rolling forecast; on demand when financing is evaluated
typical_duration: agent: 1 to 2 hours; waiting: lender or manufacturer response time for financing evaluation

name: Capital raising, investor and lender reporting, and insurance
trigger: on demand (raise or loan process) | monthly (reporting) | quarterly (board deck) | annually (insurance renewal) | event: insured loss
human_role: the person assembling the data room and the cover
inputs_required: brand brain: cap table, prior raises, insurance policies

steps.name: Assemble the data room
steps.does: Assemble the recurring documents a lender or investor asks for: financials, cohort economics, cap table, contracts.
steps.check: every document in the room has a version date

steps.name: Produce the recurring reporting pack
steps.does: Produce the monthly update, covenant compliance check and quarterly board deck financials from existing outputs.
steps.check: covenant compliance is stated as met or breached, never implied

steps.name: Identify required insurance coverage
steps.does: Identify the coverage an e-commerce brand needs: product liability, cyber, business owner's policy, and D&O once there are outside investors.
steps.check: each coverage type states why it applies to this brand

steps.name: Compare quotes
steps.does: Compare insurance quotes against the coverage checklist and the brand's own risk profile.
steps.check: premium, deductible and exclusions are shown side by side, not just premium

steps.name: Track the renewal date
steps.does: Track the renewal date for every active policy and flag it before the window closes.
steps.check: no policy renews without a flag at least 30 days ahead

steps.name: Prepare a claim on a loss event
steps.does: When a loss occurs, prepare the claim with the evidence the insurer asks for (transit, stock, cyber or product liability) and track it to resolution.
steps.check: the claim cites the exact policy clause it is filed under
steps.ask_founder_if: the loss involves a customer injury or a data breach needing legal review

steps.name: Write the founder brief and stop
steps.does: Write the recommendation on financing, coverage or a claim outcome and stop for approval before any commitment.
steps.check: no financing, coverage or claim decision is treated as final by this agent
steps.ask_founder_if: always: these are founder_gate or human_assist capabilities

qa: every document version-dated
covenant status stated plainly
claim evidence matches the exact policy clause
read_point: monthly for reporting; annually for renewal; on the claim's resolution date
typical_duration: agent: 1 to 2 hours per cycle; waiting: lender, investor or insurer turnaround

name: Report unit economics and plan the growth budget
trigger: weekly (CAC, LTV, revenue forecast) | monthly (OPEX budget, MMM refresh)
human_role: the growth finance lead
inputs_required: orders with cohort and channel tags

steps.name: Screen orders for fraud and bots
steps.does: Screen the order set for fraud and bot-driven orders before computing any cohort number.
steps.check: flagged orders are excluded and counted, not silently dropped

steps.name: Compute the 4 labeled CACs
steps.does: Compute blended, media-only, paid and fully loaded CAC from spend and orders.
steps.check: no CAC is shown without its label

steps.name: Build cohorts and LTGP:CAC
steps.does: Build first-order cohorts, compute CAC payback and LTGP:CAC against the metric contract's fixed bands.
steps.output: cohort table with payback and LTGP:CAC
steps.check: LTV is gross profit, never revenue

steps.name: Gate acquisition scale-up
steps.does: Gate any acquisition scale-up recommendation on first-order economics, not blended averages.
steps.check: the recommendation names the cohort it is based on

steps.name: Forecast revenue from separate inputs
steps.does: Forecast new-customer and returning revenue separately from the spend-efficiency curve, cohort repeat rate and the dated marketing calendar.
steps.check: short histories are regressed to the mean, never extrapolated straight-line

steps.name: Build subscription unit economics
steps.does: If the brand has subscriptions, build churn against the correct prior-period base, conservative lifetime estimates, and prepaid-plan economics.
steps.check: churn denominator is the correct prior-period base, not total customers

steps.name: Build the annual budget
steps.does: Build the annual budget separate from the rolling forecast, sizing OPEX and payroll to the brand's own profit target.
steps.check: OPEX is sized to the profit target, not last year's spend plus a percent

steps.name: Answer the marginal spend question
steps.does: Answer marginal spend questions (the next 10,000 dollars) by ranking channels on CM3 and CAC payback.
steps.check: the ranking is computed in code, never asserted in prose

steps.name: Cross-check with an MMM read where relevant
steps.does: Where blended MER and platform ROAS keep disagreeing, cross-check the scenario ranking against a marketing mix read.
steps.check: the note states agreement or the size of the gap, never silently picks one number

steps.name: Publish the weekly and monthly outputs
steps.does: Publish CAC/LTV and revenue forecast weekly, and the OPEX budget and subscription economics monthly.
steps.check: every figure states its window and freshness

qa: LTV always gross profit
no channel-level CAC presented as a finance number
scale gate based on first-order cohort, not blended
read_point: weekly for CAC/LTV/forecast; monthly for budget, against the annual target
typical_duration: agent: 1.5 to 2.5 hours per full run

name: GST, HSN and tax compliance tracking
trigger: monthly, before GST return filing | event: new SKU or B2B dispatch
human_role: the person tracking GST and tax compliance
inputs_required: brand brain: selling markets, SKU list
stock transfer and B2B dispatch log
gift card and loyalty point ledger

steps.name: Assign and validate HSN or SAC codes
steps.does: Build and keep the SKU-to-HSN/SAC map correct for every SKU, since a wrong or too-short code is a common cause of e-invoice portal rejections.
steps.check: no SKU ships without a validated code

steps.name: Track GST nexus and registration thresholds
steps.does: Track GST or sales-tax nexus and registration thresholds per market the brand sells into.
steps.output: nexus and threshold status by market
steps.check: a market crossing a threshold is flagged before the filing deadline, not after

steps.name: Prepare GSTR-1 and 3B inputs
steps.does: Prepare the sales and input-credit data GSTR-1 and 3B need, and match input credit against GSTR-2B.
steps.check: every mismatch between claimed and GSTR-2B credit is listed, not netted away

steps.name: Claim marketplace TCS and TDS credit
steps.does: Reconcile TCS collected by marketplaces under Section 52 and TDS deducted against the credit actually available.
steps.check: credit claimed never exceeds what the marketplace's own statement supports

steps.name: Raise e-way bills
steps.does: Raise e-way bills for B2B dispatch and stock transfer above the threshold value.
steps.check: every dispatch above threshold has a matching e-way bill number

steps.name: Reconcile GST credit notes against returns
steps.does: Check that every completed return or refund has a matching GST credit note issued and filed on time.
steps.check: a refund without a matching credit note is flagged before the return period closes

steps.name: Book liabilities correctly
steps.does: Book gift cards and loyalty points as liabilities recognized on redemption, and track FX exposure separately from GST.
steps.check: gift cards are never recognized as revenue at sale

steps.name: Hand off filing to the accountant
steps.does: Package GSTR-1, 3B inputs, credit reconciliation and e-way bill log for the brand's accountant to file.
steps.check: the package states what this agent tracked versus what filing itself still needs a person
steps.ask_founder_if: always: actual GST return filing stays with the brand's accountant

qa: no SKU without a validated HSN/SAC code
TCS and GST on fees never netted
filing itself stays human, tracking is agent_does
read_point: monthly, ahead of the filing deadline
typical_duration: agent: 1 to 1.5 hours; waiting: accountant filing turnaround

name: Run the cash operations cycle: payables, receivables, payroll and expense
trigger: on bill receipt and weekly aging (AP) | on invoice due date and weekly aging (AR) | monthly payroll cycle | monthly card cycle (expense)
human_role: the accounts operations person
inputs_required: brand brain: approval chain by amount and vendor

steps.name: Capture every vendor bill
steps.does: Capture every incoming vendor bill and match it to its purchase order and goods receipt.
steps.check: every bill has a matching PO and receipt or is flagged unmatched

steps.name: Route AP approval
steps.does: Route each matched bill through the approval chain by amount and vendor, and schedule payment on the agreed terms.
steps.output: AP approval queue and payment schedule
steps.check: no bill is scheduled for payment without its approval step complete

steps.name: Run the AP aging review
steps.does: Run the weekly aging review on unpaid bills and flag anything approaching a late-payment penalty.
steps.check: every bill nearing its due date is flagged at least 3 days ahead

steps.name: Invoice wholesale and B2B buyers
steps.does: Invoice wholesale and B2B buyers on their agreed terms.
steps.check: every invoice states its due date from the agreed terms, never a default

steps.name: Track AR to collection
steps.does: Track every invoice from issue to collection and run a structured dunning sequence on anything overdue.
steps.check: the dunning sequence follows a fixed schedule, not an ad hoc reminder

steps.name: Process payroll
steps.does: Process payroll for the cycle from the roster and hours or salary data.
steps.check: every employee's gross-to-net calculation is shown, not just the net figure

steps.name: Prepare statutory filings
steps.does: Prepare the statutory filings that go with payroll: PF, ESI, professional tax and TDS, plus Form 16 at year end.
steps.check: every filing amount ties back to the payroll run it came from
steps.ask_founder_if: a filing needs a person's digital signature to submit

steps.name: Collect and apply the expense policy
steps.does: Collect receipts for every reimbursable expense and corporate card charge and apply the travel-and-expense policy.
steps.check: every line is marked compliant or flagged against the written policy

steps.name: Reconcile the card statement
steps.does: Reconcile the corporate card statement to the ledger.
steps.check: every statement line matches a ledger entry or is flagged

steps.name: Publish the cash operations summary
steps.does: Publish one summary of AP aging, AR aging, payroll cost and expense compliance for the cycle.
steps.check: every number states its cycle and freshness

outputs: issued B2B invoices and AR aging
payroll run and statutory filing pack
qa: approval chain enforced by amount and vendor
payroll gross-to-net always shown, not only net
expense policy applied line by line
read_point: weekly for AP/AR aging; monthly for payroll and card cycle
typical_duration: agent: 1.5 to 2 hours per cycle; waiting: bank payment runs and card statement date

name: Set and reconcile partner, affiliate and creator commercial terms
trigger: each payout cycle | event: a commission tier change is proposed | event: creator deal agreed | weekly check of live posts
human_role: the partnerships finance lead
inputs_required: brand brain: partner tiers, product category margins, customer status rules
live creator and affiliate post list

steps.name: Set commission rates
steps.does: Set commission rates by partner type, product category and customer status (new versus returning), so margin is protected on every payout.
steps.check: no commission rate is set without checking the category's own CM

steps.name: Reconcile the affiliate network statement
steps.does: Reconcile what the affiliate network says is owed against actual delivered, non-returned orders.
steps.check: a returned or cancelled order never carries a paid commission

steps.name: Approve the payout
steps.does: Approve the reconciled payout amount before it is sent.
steps.check: the payout amount matches the reconciliation exactly
steps.ask_founder_if: always: commission tiers and payouts are founder_gate

steps.name: Keep the creator agreement template current
steps.does: Keep one creator agreement template current: deliverables, usage rights, exclusivity, payment terms and the disclosure clause.
steps.check: the disclosure clause matches the current ASCI guideline

steps.name: Check live posts for disclosure
steps.does: Check live creator and affiliate posts weekly for the ASCI and platform disclosure tags the agreement requires.
steps.check: every non-compliant post is listed with the platform and the missing tag

steps.name: Flag non-compliance
steps.does: Flag any creator or affiliate post missing disclosure to the founder for a takedown or correction request.
steps.check: each flag names the specific rule the post breaks
steps.ask_founder_if: a repeat offender needs the agreement itself reviewed

qa: commission never paid on a returned order
disclosure checked against the current ASCI rule
payout never sent without approval
read_point: each payout cycle, against the reconciliation; weekly for disclosure checks
typical_duration: agent: 45 minutes to 1.5 hours per cycle

name: Audit tracking across a surface
trigger: monthly, rotating by surface | event: new account, quarterly recheck, or after a major site or app change
human_role: the analytics engineer running the tracking audit

steps.name: Pick the surface
steps.does: Pick the surface to audit this run: GA4, Meta pixel and CAPI, Google Ads, or server events, by trigger or by the standing rotation.
steps.check: the surface picked matches the trigger, not a guess

steps.name: Pull the surface's live config
steps.does: Pull the live configuration for the chosen surface: GA4 property/stream settings, or the Meta pixel/CAPI setup, or Google Ads conversion actions, or the server-side tag container.
steps.check: the export is dated and matches the currently published version

steps.name: Run the surface-specific audit
steps.does: Run the fixed checklist for that surface: GA4 property/stream structure, timezone, retention, consent and key events; or Meta dedup, event match quality and consent gating; or Google Ads primary conversion action and enhanced conversions; or server-side container structure and duplicate tags.
steps.check: every checklist item is marked pass, fail or unavailable, none skipped

steps.name: Verify event-to-standard-event mapping
steps.does: Verify every store event maps to the surface's own standard event or key event, with value passed through.
steps.check: every store event has a mapped standard event or is flagged unmapped

steps.name: Test in the surface's own debug tool
steps.does: Test the live setup in DebugView, Meta's Test Events tool, or the Google Ads diagnostics tab as the surface requires.
steps.check: the test uses a real test transaction, not only a config read

steps.name: Build the ranked fix list
steps.does: Build a ranked fix list: the exact current setting, the exact proposed setting, and whether it needs founder approval or a person to apply it.
steps.check: every fix row names the surface it touches

steps.name: Compare to the last audit
steps.does: Compare this audit to the last one run on the same surface and flag anything that regressed.
steps.check: a regression is flagged even if the current state still passes

steps.name: Hand off the fix list
steps.does: Hand the fix list to a developer or the founder, since this agent never applies a tracking change itself.
steps.check: no tracking configuration was changed by this agent
steps.ask_founder_if: a fix needs a person with admin access to the ad account or the tag manager

qa: one property or pixel per journey confirmed
internal traffic filtered
no page_view marked as a key event
read_point: monthly per surface; immediately after any major site or app change
typical_duration: agent: 45 to 75 minutes per surface
subagents: money-security-scanner shares log access for the server-events surface only

name: Enforce UTM discipline and reconcile attribution models
trigger: monthly | trigger: platform ROAS and blended MER keep disagreeing, or a budget review
human_role: the analytics engineer keeping attribution honest
inputs_required: every existing paid and owned link
GA4, Meta, Shopify and marketplace order counts

steps.name: Write or confirm the UTM convention
steps.does: Write one UTM convention (source, medium, campaign, content, term) or confirm the existing one is still followed.
steps.check: every parameter has a fixed, documented value set

steps.name: Audit every existing link
steps.does: Audit every existing paid and owned link against the convention.
steps.check: every non-conforming link is listed with its exact fix

steps.name: Clean fake organic and direct rows
steps.does: Clean fake organic or direct rows out of campaign tables caused by missing or broken UTMs before anyone reads them.
steps.check: no channel table is published with a known UTM leak still in it

steps.name: Cross-check order counts
steps.does: Cross-check GA4, Meta, Shopify and marketplace order counts against each other and against store orders for the period.
steps.check: every gap over 2 percent has a named cause

steps.name: Flag bot-driven spikes
steps.does: Flag any spike in one platform's order or session count that does not match store orders, as a possible bot signal.
steps.check: a flagged spike is handed to the security scan before anyone reacts to it

steps.name: Report the attribution model gap
steps.does: Report the gap between attribution models (last-click versus data-driven, platform versus GA4) per channel.
steps.check: the gap is shown per channel, never as one blended number

steps.name: Run or schedule a holdout test
steps.does: Before a big reallocation call, run or schedule a holdout test rather than trust the attribution gap alone.
steps.check: the test result, once available, is cited by its own confidence interval

steps.name: Evaluate a third-party attribution stack if warranted
steps.does: When platform ROAS and blended MER keep disagreeing after reconciliation, decide whether a paid attribution or MMM tool is worth its cost against the brand's own blended-MER and lift-test approach.
steps.output: MMM stack evaluation with a recommendation
steps.check: the recommendation compares tool cost to the brand's own current accuracy, not vendor claims alone
steps.ask_founder_if: the decision commits to a recurring paid subscription

steps.name: Document the attribution convention
steps.does: Document which model the brand uses for which decision, so nobody reads a number without knowing its source model.
steps.check: the convention states which model governs budget decisions

qa: no channel table published with a known UTM leak
bot spikes flagged before anyone reacts
MMM tool judged against the brand's own lift tests
read_point: monthly for UTM and cross-check; on the trigger for MMM evaluation
typical_duration: agent: 1 to 1.5 hours; waiting: holdout test read window if one is run

name: Build the post-purchase attribution survey
trigger: event: building or refreshing the attribution model | event: a new high-spend channel needs proof it works
human_role: the analytics engineer adding a zero-party data source
inputs_required: brand brain: product lines, customer types

steps.name: Draft the one question
steps.does: Draft the one-question, thank-you-page survey: how did you hear about us.
steps.check: the question is one sentence, plain language

steps.name: Branch the answer options
steps.does: Branch the answer options by product or customer type where the channel mix differs.
steps.check: every branch maps to a channel the brand actually runs

steps.name: Place it on the thank-you page
steps.does: Prepare the placement spec for the thank-you page as a developer brief, since this agent does not write site code.
steps.check: the spec names the exact page and does not touch checkout

steps.name: Set the sample and response window
steps.does: Set the sample size and response window needed for the answers to be usable.
